answer: A farm running 170 keys therefore pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation inexpensive. Because the ledge stake is held until the yarrow settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the summit audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 15% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a low-cost one. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
